answer: Sybil resistance can be built as a climbable bond terrace: a first identity posts a modest lock, but each extra account sharing a funding graph or hardware fingerprint must post a geometrically larger bond, so a farm's cost spiral quickly outruns any vote it could buy. Admission is gated by a short, randomized liveness pulse in which every claimant must answer a unique work challenge at the same clock; clones spun up after the pulse miss the window and forfeit the lock. Cheap throwaways never clear the first terrace, and coordinated batches stall on the spiral before they settle.
